liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (2 reviews): A 40-foot dragon danced through the crowd, then the band erupted into a thrashing Other One; Opening is lovely, but after the first chorus the jam slides downhill, though still a great version [10][11]
- **The Mighty Quinn** (1 review): Reviewer finds Quinn pretty good [11]
- **Samson and Delilah** (1 review): Solid, punchy and pounding; avoids the too-fast, distorted-note problem of other versions [12]
- **Smokestack Lightning** (1 review): Weir roars; reviewer calls it one of the best Brent-era Smokestacks [12]
- **Comes A Time** (1 review): Described as tender, following a stormy Other One [12]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Reviewer recalls an incredible He's Gone into Smokestack, then Comes A Time, before heading to the floor during drums [17]
- **Drums** (1 review): Drums section is monstrous and really psychedelic, the best part of the show [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd86-02-09 t01 Crowd Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-09 t02 Jack Straw**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-09 t03 They Love Each Other**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-09 t04 CC Rider**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-09 t05 Loser**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-09 t06 Man Smart (Woman Smarter)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-09 t07 Deal**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd86-02-09 t08 Crowd Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-02-09.140206.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 122 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1986-02-09.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.106119.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 119 min; rated 2.67/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: Hot but patchy show; Garcia sounds ill [21]
- **gd1986-02-09.138525.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 17 songs; 117 min [4]
- **gd1986-02-09.schoeps.oade.gems.74135.flac16**: source not stated; 17 songs; 120 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [7]. Said about its sound: Excellent recording; the performance has nice moments alongside some slips and drops [16]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended the whole run including Mardi Gras; found this the best of the four nights, very psychedelic [10]
- Midway through second set, a man in Chinese dress sprayed a fire extinguisher, and a 40-foot dragon danced through the crowd [14]
- Reviewer was a sailor attending alone on a friend's ticket; this was his second show [14]
- A Chinese band played Chinese music before the show, as at the previous night's Chinese New Year show [17]
- The run coincided with Chinese New Year, Valentine's Day and Mardi Gras [18]
- Chinese drummers played on a platform above the stage during the show, with spotlights flashing [19]
- Judged best of the four-night run (five counting Valentine's Day); criticizes short show, six-song first set and 74-minute second [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-02-09.140206.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Oade; transferred by Charlie Miller, Jim Wise, Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: (FOB) Schoeps CMC4/MK41 > Oade M118 > Sony PCM-F1; Transfer Info: Master Oade PCM (unknown deck/hardware/software) > hard disk > Adobe Audition… [1]
